projectCategory: DSA Module 6.3: Fenwick Trees & B-Tree Storage Architecture
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: 1D Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick Tree) Point Update & Prefix Sum Query
projects.description: A Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree / BIT) is a compact array data structure of size `N+1` that supports point updates `arr[i] += val` and prefix sum queries `sum(arr[1..i])` in logarithmic O(log N) time using Two's Complement Bitwise Low-Bit isolations `i & -i`. In this project, you will build a 1D Fenwick Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Fenwick Tree Architecture, Bitwise Low-Bit Navigation (`i & -i`, `i += i & -i`, `i -= i & -i`) & Logarithmic Sums
projects.exampleText: Update values and query prefix sum [1..4]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 1D Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) ---
Prefix Sum [1..4] (1+3+5+7) = 16
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Point Update**: Loop `idx += idx & -idx` adds `val` to responsible BIT cells.
2. **Prefix Query**: Loop `idx -= idx & -idx` subtracts lowest set bit to aggregate prefix sum.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_bit()` & `query_prefix_sum()`: Implements point updates and prefix sum queries in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Range Sum Query using 1D Fenwick Tree (query(R) - query(L-1))
projects.description: Compute range sum over ANY arbitrary subarray `[L .. R]` using a 1D Fenwick Tree in logarithmic O(log N) time! Formula: `range_sum(L, R) = prefix_sum(R) - prefix_sum(L - 1)`. In this project, you will build Range Sum Query Fenwick Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Subarray Sum Invariants, Prefix Difference Formulas & Constant Memory Range Queries
projects.exampleText: Query range sum [2..4] for [0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Sum Query using 1D Fenwick Tree ---
Range Sum [2..4] (4+6+8) = 18
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Difference**: Subtract prefix sum `L-1` from prefix sum `R`.
2. **Logarithmic Bounds**: Requires only 2 prefix queries of O(log N) steps.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `query_range_sum()`: Computes subarray range sum using prefix differences.

projects.title: Fenwick Tree Range Update and Point Query (diff array fenwick)
projects.description: Support Range Addition updates `arr[L..R] += val` and Point Queries `query(idx)` in O(log N) time! Maintain a difference array inside the Fenwick Tree: update `L` with `+val` and `R+1` with `-val`. Point query `query(idx)` returns the exact value of `arr[idx]`! In this project, you will build Range Update Point Query BIT in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Difference Array BIT Invariants, Range Additions & Point Query Recoveries
projects.exampleText: Apply range update +10 to [2..5] and query point 3
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fenwick Tree Range Update & Point Query ---
Value at Index 3 after +10 update to [2..5] = 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Range Update**: `update_diff(L, val)` and `update_diff(R + 1, -val)`.
2. **Point Query**: `point_query(idx)` returns prefix sum of difference array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_update()` & `point_query()`: Executes range updates and point queries using difference BIT.

projects.title: Range Update and Range Query Fenwick Tree (Dual BITs)
projects.description: Support BOTH Range Updates `arr[L..R] += val` AND Range Sum Queries `sum(L, R)` in O(log N) time using TWO Fenwick Trees `BIT1` and `BIT2`! Formula: `sum(1..i) = query(BIT1, i) * i - query(BIT2, i)`. In this project, you will build Dual BIT Range Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Fenwick Tree Architecture, Range Multiplication Formulas & O(log N) Dual Operations
projects.exampleText: Update range [2..6] += 5 and query range sum [3..5]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Update and Range Query Fenwick Tree (Dual BITs) ---
Applied +5 update to [2..6]. Range Sum Query [3..5] = 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **BIT1 Update**: Update `L` with `val` and `R+1` with `-val`.
2. **BIT2 Update**: Update `L` with `val * (L - 1)` and `R+1` with `-val * R`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dual_fenwick_demo()`: Solves range updates and range queries using dual BITs.

projects.title: Count Smaller Numbers After Self using Fenwick Tree
projects.description: Given integer array `nums`, count for each element `nums[i]` how many smaller elements exist to its right (`j > i`). Iterate array from right to left, query prefix count `query_prefix(nums[i] - 1)` on frequency Fenwick Tree, then update `update_bit(nums[i], 1)` in O(N log N) time! In this project, you will build Count Smaller After Self Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Right-to-Left Array Sweeps, Frequency BIT Lookups & Inversion Sub-Counting
projects.exampleText: Count smaller numbers after self for [5, 2, 6, 1]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Smaller Numbers After Self (Fenwick Tree) ---
Counts for [5, 2, 6, 1]: [ 2, 1, 1, 0 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Right-to-Left Traversal**: Process elements from right end.
2. **Prefix Query**: `query_prefix(val - 1)` counts numbers smaller than `val` seen to right.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_smaller_after_self_demo()`: Counts smaller numbers after self using Fenwick Tree.

projects.title: B-Tree Node Structure & Degree Order Properties
projects.description: A B-Tree is a self-balancing M-way search tree designed for disk storage systems. For minimum degree T: 1) Every node (except root) contains at least `T-1` keys and at most `2T-1` keys; 2) Internal nodes have at most `2T` children; 3) All leaves are at the exact same depth! In this project, you will build B-Tree Structural Layout in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree Formal Definitions, Degree Order Bounds (T-1 to 2T-1 Keys) & Leaf Depth Invariants
projects.exampleText: Initialize B-Tree node of degree T=3
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Node Structure & Degree Order Properties ---
Created B-Tree node of degree T=3 (Max Keys = 5, Max Children = 6)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Key Array**: Node holds sorted keys array of size `2T-1`.
2. **Children Pointers**: Node holds children pointers array of size `2T`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `main()`: Defines and validates B-Tree node structure properties.

projects.title: B-Tree Key Insertion & Child Splitting Mechanics
projects.description: Insert keys into B-Tree. When attempting to insert into a full node containing `2T - 1` keys, split the child into two nodes of `T - 1` keys each and promote the median key up to the parent node in O(T log_T N) time! In this project, you will build B-Tree Insertion Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree Node Splitting, Median Key Promotion & Proactive Pre-Splitting
projects.exampleText: Insert 6 keys into B-Tree of degree T=3
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Key Insertion & Child Splitting ---
Inserted 6 keys. Full node split into 2 child nodes with median key promoted to parent.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Proactive Split**: Split full children during down-traversal to prevent cascading splits.
2. **Median Promotion**: Promote `keys[T-1]` to parent.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_insert_split_demo()`: Executes B-Tree key insertion with node splitting.

projects.title: B-Tree Key Search Engine
projects.description: Search for a target key inside a B-Tree. Perform binary search (or linear search) inside current node's sorted `keys` array. If key is not found, recurse down to child index `i` in `O(T log_T N)` time! In this project, you will build B-Tree Key Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree Search Traversal, Node Key Binary Search & Depth-Bound Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Search key 42 in B-Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Key Search Engine ---
Search Key 42 in B-Tree: FOUND at Depth 2.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Node Key Search**: Find smallest index `i` where `key <= keys[i]`.
2. **Child Recurse**: If `keys[i] != key`, recurse search on `children[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_search_demo()`: Solves B-Tree key search.

projects.title: B-Tree Key Deletion & Merging/Borrowing Operations
projects.description: Delete a key from B-Tree. If deletion causes node key count to drop below `T - 1` (Underflow): 1) Borrow key from sibling if sibling has `>= T` keys; 2) Merge with sibling node if sibling has `T - 1` keys. Maintains balance! In this project, you will build B-Tree Deletion Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree Deletion Rules, Sibling Key Borrowing & Node Merging Mechanics
projects.exampleText: Delete key 20 causing node underflow
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Key Deletion & Merging/Borrowing ---
Deleted key 20. Borrowed sibling key to prevent node underflow.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Borrow Key**: Transfer key from rich sibling via parent.
2. **Merge Nodes**: Combine underflowed node with sibling and parent median key.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_delete_demo()`: Solves B-Tree key deletion with borrowing and merging.

projects.title: B+ Tree Leaf Node Linked List Traversal Engine
projects.description: In a B+ Tree, ALL data records reside EXCLUSIVELY in leaf nodes; internal nodes store only router search keys. All leaf nodes are linked sequentially via a singly/doubly linked list (`next` pointer), enabling ultra-fast range scans in O(K) time! In this project, you will build B+ Tree Leaf Traversal Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B+ Tree Leaf Sequence Sets, Linked List Leaf Traversal & Range Query Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Traverse linked list sequence set of B+ Tree leaves
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B+ Tree Leaf Node Linked List Traversal ---
Traversed leaf sequence set: [ 10 → 20 → 30 → 40 → 50 → 60 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sequence Set**: Follow `leaf->next` pointers directly.
2. **No Tree Ascent**: Eliminates tree re-traversals during range scans.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bplus_tree_leaf_traversal_demo()`: Demonstrates B+ Tree leaf linked list sequence set traversal.

projects.title: 2D Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) for Matrix Prefix Sums
projects.description: A 2D Fenwick Tree maintains a 2D matrix array `bit2d[R+1][C+1]`. Supports point updates `matrix[r][c] += val` and 2D prefix sums `sum([(1,1)..(r,c)])` in `O(log R * log C)` time! Nested low-bit loops: `for(i=r; i<=R; i+=i&-i) for(j=c; j<=C; j+=j&-j)`. In this project, you will build 2D Fenwick Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Fenwick Tree Architecture, Nested Bitwise Loops & 2D Matrix Subgrid Sum Queries
projects.exampleText: Update matrix[2][2] += 5 and query 2D prefix sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Fenwick Tree Matrix Prefix Sums ---
2D Prefix Sum [(1,1)..(2,2)] = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2D Point Update**: Outer loop updates row `i += i & -i`, inner loop updates col `j += j & -j`.
2. **2D Submatrix Sum**: `Sum = Q(r2,c2) - Q(r1-1,c2) - Q(r2,c1-1) + Q(r1-1,c1-1)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_2d()` & `query_2d()`: Implements 2D Fenwick Tree matrix operations.

projects.title: 2D Range Update and Range Query Fenwick Tree
projects.description: Support 2D Range Updates `matrix[(r1,c1)..(r2,c2)] += val` AND 2D Submatrix Sum Queries in `O(log R * log C)` time using 4 2D Fenwick Trees! In this project, you will build 2D Dual BIT Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Range Inclusion Formulas, 4-BIT Matrix Maintenance & Submatrix Range Operations
projects.exampleText: Update submatrix [(1,1)..(3,3)] += 10 and query submatrix sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Range Update and Range Query Fenwick Tree ---
Updated submatrix [(1,1)..(3,3)] += 10. Submatrix Sum Query = 90
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **4 Corner Updates**: Update `(r1,c1)`, `(r1,c2+1)`, `(r2+1,c1)`, `(r2+1,c2+1)`.
2. **2D Inclusion-Exclusion**: Combine 4 2D BIT queries for submatrix sum.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_2d_fenwick_demo()`: Solves 2D range updates and 2D range queries.

projects.title: Fenwick Tree Binary Lifting (Binary Search on BIT in O(log N))
projects.description: Find the FIRST index in array where prefix sum is `>= target` on a Fenwick Tree in optimal `O(log N)` time (instead of nested `O(log^2 N)` binary search)! Step down bit powers of two (`idx += 1 << i`) directly on the BIT array. In this project, you will build Fenwick Tree Binary Lifting Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: BIT Binary Lifting, Powers of 2 Bit Steps & O(log N) Target Index Search
projects.exampleText: Find first index with prefix sum >= 15 via BIT binary lifting
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fenwick Tree Binary Lifting (Binary Search on BIT) ---
First index with prefix sum >= 15 is Index 4 (Found in O(log N) time via Binary Lifting).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Power Step Loop**: Loop step size from MSB power of 2 down to 1 (`step >>= 1`).
2. **Bit Accumulation**: If `sum + bit[idx + step] < target`, jump `idx += step` and `sum += bit[idx]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `fenwick_binary_lifting_demo()`: Solves binary search on BIT using binary lifting.

projects.title: Coordinate Compression + Fenwick Tree for Large Value Ranges
projects.description: When element values are huge (e.g. `0 <= arr[i] <= 10^9`), create a compressed index mapping `1 .. N` by sorting unique array elements. Operates Fenwick Tree over compressed indices in `O(N log N)` space/time! In this project, you will build Coordinate Compressed Fenwick Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Coordinate Compression, Value Index Mapping & Large-Range BIT Execution
projects.exampleText: Map value range [10^2, 10^9, 10^5] to compressed indices
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Coordinate Compression + Fenwick Tree ---
Mapped large value range [10^2, 10^9, 10^5] to compressed indices [1, 3, 2]. Range Sum = 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sort & Unique**: Sort distinct array values.
2. **Binary Search Index**: `lower_bound` maps huge values to 1..N indices.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `coordinate_compressed_fenwick_demo()`: Solves large-value range queries via coordinate compression + BIT.

projects.title: Count Pairs of Inversions in Matrix using 2D Fenwick Tree
projects.description: Count 2D matrix inversion pairs `(r1 <= r2)` and `(c1 <= c2)` where `matrix[r1][c1] > matrix[r2][c2]`. Traverse 2D matrix cells in order and query 2D Fenwick Tree in `O(R * C * log R * log C)` time! In this project, you will build Matrix Inversions 2D BIT Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Matrix Inversions, 2D Frequency BIT Lookups & Spatial Inversion Pairs
projects.exampleText: Count 2D matrix inversion pairs via 2D BIT
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Inversion Pairs in Matrix via 2D Fenwick Tree ---
Total 2D Matrix Inversion Pairs Count = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2D Traversal**: Iterate matrix cells sequentially.
2. **2D BIT Frequency**: Query 2D BIT for counts of greater values encountered in preceding subgrid.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `matrix_inversion_2d_fenwick_demo()`: Counts matrix inversion pairs using 2D Fenwick Tree.

projects.title: B-Tree Disk I/O Block Access Simulator (Node Block Allocation)
projects.description: Simulate B-Tree page disk block access. Each B-Tree node is sized to match exact physical disk block size (e.g. 4096 bytes). Track total Disk Read / Write operations (Disk I/Os). Prove B-Tree performs search in `O(log_B N)` disk reads! In this project, you will build B-Tree Disk I/O Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Disk Block Layouts (4096 Bytes), Disk I/O Reduction & O(log_B N) Page Access Math
projects.exampleText: Simulate B-Tree disk block accesses for 4096-byte blocks
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Disk I/O Block Access Simulator ---
Simulated disk block allocation (4096-byte block size). Executed search in 2 disk I/O operations.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Block Padding**: Pad node struct to match 4KB page size.
2. **I/O Counter**: Increment `disk_io_reads++` whenever fetching node from disk.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_disk_io_demo()`: Simulates B-Tree disk page block allocations and I/O counts.

projects.title: B+ Tree Index File Engine (Internal Nodes + Sequence Set Leaves)
projects.description: Implement a simplified Database Index File Engine using B+ Tree architecture. Internal nodes act as routing key indexes; leaf nodes store actual data records and link to adjacent leaves via a doubly-linked list. In this project, you will build Database B+ Tree Index File Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Database Index Files, Router Key Nodes vs Data Leaves & Range Scan Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Index 100,000 database records in B+ Tree Index File
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B+ Tree Index File Engine ---
Indexed 100,000 database records in B+ Tree Index File. Data records stored in sequence set leaves.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Router Keys**: Internal nodes store copies of keys for routing search paths.
2. **Sequence Set**: Leaves store full records and linked pointers.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bplus_tree_index_file_demo()`: Solves B+ Tree database index file engine.

projects.title: Range Minimum Query (RMQ) Fenwick Tree Adaptation
projects.description: Adapt a Fenwick Tree to support Range Minimum Queries `min(arr[L..R])`. Since `min` operation is NOT invertible (unlike addition), update both tree arrays during point updates in `O(log^2 N)` time! In this project, you will build RMQ Fenwick Tree Adaptor in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Non-Invertible Operation Adaptation, Min Operation Sweeps & Fenwick RMQ Limits
projects.exampleText: Execute RMQ query via adapted Fenwick Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Minimum Query (RMQ) Fenwick Tree Adaptation ---
Executed RMQ query in O(log^2 N) time via adapted Fenwick Tree.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Non-Invertible Min**: Recalculate cell minimum by inspecting direct children during update.
2. **Query Breakdown**: Combine segment minimums in `O(log^2 N)` step iterations.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `rmq_fenwick_adaptation_demo()`: Adapts Fenwick Tree for Range Minimum Queries.

projects.title: Dynamic Frequency Median Finder using Fenwick Tree
projects.description: Find the Median of a dynamic stream of numbers in O(log N) time! Maintain number frequencies in a Fenwick Tree. Compute target rank `K = (total_elements + 1) / 2`, then use **Fenwick Tree Binary Lifting** to find index with prefix sum `K` in `O(log N)`! In this project, you will build Dynamic Stream Median Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Stream Medians, Frequency BIT Rankings & Binary Lifting Rank Search
projects.exampleText: Find dynamic median in number stream
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Frequency Median Finder via Fenwick Tree ---
Current Stream Median = 14 (Found via Fenwick Tree Binary Lifting in O(log N)).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Insertion**: Update `update_bit(val, 1)`.
2. **Binary Lifting Search**: Locate element at cumulative frequency rank `K` in O(log N).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `fenwick_median_finder_demo()`: Solves dynamic stream median using Fenwick Tree binary lifting.

projects.title: B-Tree Traversal & Range Key Search Query Engine
projects.description: Execute Range Key Searches `queryRange(minKey, maxKey)` on a B-Tree. Perform in-order traversal pruning subtrees outside key bounds `[minKey, maxKey]` in O(K + log N) time! In this project, you will build B-Tree Range Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree In-Order Traversals, Search Tree Pruning & Range Key Extractions
projects.exampleText: Find keys in range [20..50] in B-Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B-Tree Traversal & Range Key Search Query Engine ---
Keys in Range [20..50]: [ 20, 25, 30, 42, 50 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pruned Traversal**: Recurse down children only if child range overlaps `[minKey, maxKey]`.
2. **In-Order Print**: Collect keys falling within range bounds.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_range_search_demo()`: Solves B-Tree range key search queries.

projects.title: Concurrent B+ Tree Index Engine (Latch Crabbing & Lock-Free Search)
projects.description: High-performance database storage engines (MySQL InnoDB, PostgreSQL) execute thousands of concurrent read/write queries on B+ Trees using **Latch Crabbing** (coupling read/write locks down the tree path). In this project, you will build Concurrent B+ Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Latch Crabbing Concurrency Protocol, Read/Write Lock Coupling & Thread-Safe B+ Trees
projects.exampleText: Execute concurrent read/write transactions via Latch Crabbing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Concurrent B+ Tree Index Engine (Latch Crabbing) ---
Executed concurrent read/write transactions using Latch Crabbing protocol.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Latch Coupling**: Acquire child node lock before releasing parent node lock.
2. **Safe Nodes**: Release parent locks early if child node is 'safe' (will not split or merge).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `concurrent_bplus_tree_demo()`: Implements concurrent B+ Tree with Latch Crabbing protocol.

projects.title: Dynamic 3D Fenwick Tree Space Navigator
projects.description: A 3D Fenwick Tree maintains a 3D grid `bit3d[X+1][Y+1][Z+1]`. Supports 3D point updates and 3D sub-volume sum queries `[(x1,y1,z1)..(x2,y2,z2)]` in `O(log X * log Y * log Z)` time using 8-term inclusion-exclusion! In this project, you will build 3D Fenwick Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 3D Fenwick Tree Architecture, 8-Term Volume Inclusion-Exclusion & Spatial Queries
projects.exampleText: Query 3D volume sum [(0,0,0)..(4,4,4)]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic 3D Fenwick Tree Space Navigator ---
3D Box Range Volume Query [(0,0,0)..(4,4,4)] = 512
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Triple Nested BIT**: 3 nested loops update row, col, and depth.
2. **8-Term Inclusion-Exclusion**: Combines 8 3D prefix queries for 3D box volume sum.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `fenwick_3d_demo()`: Solves 3D box volume queries using 3D Fenwick Tree.

projects.title: B* Tree Redistribution & High-Density Node Packing Engine
projects.description: A B* Tree is a B-Tree variant that delays node splitting by redistributing keys between 2 adjacent sibling nodes. Guarantees a minimum node fill factor of 66% (2/3 full) instead of 50% (1/2 full) in standard B-Trees! In this project, you will build B* Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B* Tree Architecture, Sibling Key Redistribution & 66% Minimum Fill Factor Packing
projects.exampleText: Achieve 85% node fill factor via B* Tree key redistribution
projects.exampleOutput:
--- B* Tree Redistribution & High-Density Node Packing ---
Achieved 85% minimum node fill factor using B* Tree sibling key redistribution.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2-to-3 Node Split**: Split 2 full sibling nodes into 3 nodes of 2/3 fill factor each.
2. **Fill Optimization**: Increases RAM cache utilization by packing keys densely.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bstar_tree_demo()`: Implements B* Tree high-density node packing.

projects.title: Cache-Conscious B-Tree (B-Tree SIMD Layout for RAM Caches)
projects.description: Align B-Tree node structures to match exact 64-byte L1 CPU cache line boundaries. Use SIMD vector instructions to search node keys concurrently in 1 CPU instruction cycle! In this project, you will build Cache-Conscious B-Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: CPU Cache Line Alignment (64 Bytes), SIMD Vector Node Searches & L1/L2 Cache Optimization
projects.exampleText: Search 64-byte cache line aligned node keys via SIMD
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cache-Conscious B-Tree (B-Tree SIMD Layout) ---
Executed 64-byte L1 CPU cache line aligned node binary searches in 1 SIMD instruction pass.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **64-Byte Alignment**: `alignas(64)` aligns node keys array to L1 CPU cache line.
2. **SIMD Vector Pass**: Search all keys in node concurrently using vector comparisons.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cache_conscious_btree_demo()`: Solves cache-conscious B-Tree with SIMD vector alignment.

projects.title: Memory-Mapped High-Throughput Relational Database B+ Tree Index Kernel
projects.description: Industrial database storage engines (SQLite, BerkeleyDB) implement B+ Trees over memory-mapped page files (`mmap`), executing 500,000 ACID transactions per second with write-ahead logging (WAL). In this project, you will build Database B+ Tree Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Database B+ Trees, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) & High-Throughput ACID Engine
projects.exampleText: Execute 500,000 ACID transactions/sec on disk-backed B+ Tree
projects.exampleOutput:

Processed 500,000 ACID transactions/sec on disk-backed B+ Tree storage engine.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **mmap Page Management**: Map database page files into RAM virtual address space.
2. **WAL Logging**: Log page mutations to Write-Ahead Log before committing to B+ Tree.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `db_bplus_kernel_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput database B+ Tree storage engine kernel.
